title: The Coil Torque Bench
summary: Find the torque on a coil, its magnetic moment, the energy of a dipole and the far field of a loop.
subject: physics
ncertRef: Section 4.9, Torque on current loop, magnetic dipole
learningOutcome: The student can find the torque on a coil and its magnetic moment, use energy to find how fast a coil swings, say which orientations are stable, and find the far field of a loop.

levels.title: Torque on a coil
levels.adds: Baseline: τ = NIAB sin θ for a coil whose normal makes an angle θ with the field (Ex 4.9).
hints: The area of a square coil is the side squared, in m².
τ = N I A B sin θ, with θ the angle between the normal and the field.

levels.title: Moment and shape
levels.adds: New idea: the moment m = NIA, and the torque does not depend on the shape of the coil (Ex 4.13).
hints: The magnetic moment is N I A, with A in m².
The torque is mB sin θ.
Only the area counts, not the outline of the coil.

levels.title: Swing into line
levels.adds: More steps: the torque does work as the coil turns, giving its kinetic energy of rotation (Example 4.10).
hints: At release the moment is at 90° to the field, so the torque is mB.
The work done turning through 90° is mB.
Set ½Jω² = mB to find the angular speed.

levels.title: Energy of a dipole
levels.adds: New idea: U = −mB cos θ, with stable equilibrium at θ = 0 and unstable at θ = 180° (Example 4.11).
hints: U = −mB cos θ. The work is the change in U from θ = 0.
Equilibrium needs zero torque: θ = 0 or 180°.
At θ = 0 the energy is a minimum (stable); at 180° a maximum (unstable).

levels.title: Far away
levels.adds: Apply it: a small loop is a magnetic dipole, with B on the axis twice B on the equator at the same distance (Section 4.9).
hints: First find the magnetic moment m = N I A.
On the equatorial line B is half of that.

misconceptions: The torque on a coil depends on the shape of its outline
The torque is greatest when the normal is along the field
A dipole at 180° to the field is in stable equilibrium
The magnetic moment of a loop does not depend on the number of turns
